issue_context.title: The stop words are ignored by Meili
issue_context.body:
It seems that Meili is ignoring the stop words I set. According to the [specification](https://specs.meilisearch.dev/specifications/text/0123-stop-words-setting-api.html#_3-functional-specification), stop words should be ignored in the search query during matching. However, it appears that Meili is either not handling this as expected, or I may have misunderstood the concept of stop words.

I use the following command to update the settings of the index (which contains about 2000 items):
```
curl -X PATCH "${SEARCH_SERVER_URL}/indexes/${INDEX_NAME}/settings/" -H  'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization: Bearer ${SEARCH_SERVER_KEY}" --data-binary @${SETTINGS_FILE}
```

The content of ${SETTINGS_FILE} file is following:
```
{
  "rankingRules": [
    "words",
    "typo",
    "proximity",
    "attribute",
    "sort",
    "exactness",
    "released:desc",
    "rank:desc"
  ],
  "searchableAttributes": [
    "asset_name",
    "asset_id",
    "title",
    "description",
    "actors",
    "director",
    "program_type",
    "creation_date",
    "released",
    "year",
    "suggested_price",
    "genre",
    "series_name"
  ],
  "stopWords": [
    "the",
    "a",
    "an"
  ],
  "filterableAttributes": [
    "program_type",
    "season",
    "episode",
    "actors",
    "suggested_price",
    "rated",
    "language",
    "display_as_new",
    "display_as_last_chance",
    "year",
    "director"
  ],
  "sortableAttributes": [
    "title",
    "released"
  ],
  "typoTolerance": {
    "disableOnAttributes": [
      "asset_id",
      "genre"
    ]
  }
}
```

Example of JSON items for index:
```
    {
        "asset_name": "The Launch",
        "creation_date": "29 May 2020",
        "description": "Four-star general Mark Naird - leader of the newly created Space Force - is pressured to launch a satellite despite dire warnings from scientists.",
        "asset_class": "episode",
        "title": "The Launch",
        "genre": [
            "comedy"
        ],
        "director": "Paul King",
        "actors": [
            "Steve Carell",
            "John Malkovich",
            "Ben Schwartz"
        ],
        "season": 1,
        "episode": 1,
        "year": 2020,
        "rated": "TV-MA",
        "released": "29 May 2020",
        "language": "en",
        "runtime": "35 min",
        "imdbrating": 6.8,
        "imdbvote": "N/A",
        "licensing_window_start": "2023-08-06",
        "licensing_window_end": "2027-01-20",
        "preview_period": 30,
        "display_as_new": "N",
        "display_as_last_chance": "N",
        "audio_type": "AC3",
        "hdcontent": "Y",
        "maximum_viewing_length": "48:00",
        "series_name": "Space Force",
        "subtitle_languages": "en",
        "closed_captioning": "Y",
        "suggested_price": 0.0,
        "program_type": "episode"
    },
```

The settings, aside from stopWords, seem to be working correctly, as I can see their effect in the Meili Web UI. For example, if some field is not included in searchableAttributes, the search results do not return matching items for that field when a query is executed. Meili logs also do not contain any errors during the settings are applied.

As you can see, I have set "the," "a," and "an" as stop words. However, in the screenshot below, when the search query contains these words, results are still returned. I expect that when a stop word is set, Meili would exclude the corresponding items from the results during the search query execution (and avoid highlighting them too).

**Screenshots**
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e457186f-dc56-4aa7-a2f2-bf5f8773f7b4)


**Meilisearch version:**
v1.10.2

Hello @tysonite,
I managed to reproduce the bug locally, this occurs when doing a prefix search on a stop word, I may find a fix next week for the next release,

Thank you for the report!

I came across this issue as well and noticed that this has something to do with Meilis prefix search. Searching for `"the"` and `"the "` has very different results. In the latter case, it's apparent that its treated as a stop word. I suppose Meili still needs to search for stop words at the end of the query (since they might be a valid prefix), but should ignore matches where the supposed prefix matches the whole world (e.g. if the word in the document is `the`).
